PurrPaws For LIfe

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Two weeks ago, an animals shelter South of Joburg burnt down - animals died, and donated began flowing in. But now allegations of years of serious abuse and,now, arson are swirling around the centre.

Unique Selling Point:
Carte Blanche investigates whether PurrPaws for life owner - Lindi van Rooyen - made hundreds of animals suffer years of abuse from willful neglect (2012-2019) - and then decided to end it all by setting her house on fire. We all know her story - on Jan 30 2019, it was reported that the shelter at PurrPaws burnt down killing roughly 30 animals, call for the public to come save the animals and make donations came in. Roughly a million is account for with online postings, but since then she has gotten rid of almost 800 animals. Allegations then began by various shelters who received these animals - that there were not neutered, were pregnant, were badly injured, were very diseased, malnourished. The questions began - how did the fire start, why did lindie have so much time to remove her personal animals from the house, her furniture, her TV etc, First responders said the workers said she was seen where the fire started shortly before it went up in flames, and that they had been sent to fix a fence at the bottom of the garden. Neighbours said she often wasn't there, and neglected the animals - often hiding injured/sick ones from the SPCA when they came for inspections. Turns out the SPCA have been investigating her for years responding to numerous complaints.

Summary:
The SPCA has given us access to their files on her - years of abuse from 2012 - January 2019 - the warnings range from serious abuse - animals that are sick not getting veterinary care, hundreds of animals being put down etc continual sickness amongst animals - especially cats (snuffles, oozing eyes etc), dogs fighting and malnourished - she often has numerous dogs in different cages who fight and are then mortally injured. There are warnings (all acknowledged and signed by her) that show the issues brought up after the fire have been going on for years. Shortly after the fire Kitten and Cat rescue gave evidence of serious abuse of the cats - those photo's were posted by the SPCA in response to the public asking why they had not stepped in. Turns out they were intending to shut her down before the mysterious fire. About the fire - Lindie says it was caused in the upstairs linen room by rats chewing cables, but arson investigators were called to the scene. We will ask the police for an update on that investigation. Turns out, it wasn't the rescue centre that was on fire, but her personal house.

Further information:
So her personal house shares all elec and water etc with the shelter, she has no books and has never produced even vet bills to the SPCA. When asked about it, she says she'll send them, but never does. She has received thousands of donations, but now has gotten rid of the majority of the animals. I went undercover and she said she will not close down, and will continue with the shelter, she told me she's highly allergic to cats, yet managed to get roughly 50-70 out of the house (living in the house) into cages before the fire?!? Against the vet's orders she has placed all the cats back into diseased cages, where non-diseased cats can get sick. She had continued operating and said she would continue regardless of the SPCA's allegations. She says she is being targeted by them, and that the animals were injured before they came. Numerous reports, evidence from numerous animal organizations and insider information all say and show otherwise. In fact, she asked for money as a donation so she can rebuild and reopen. She cannot say she didn't know because she has the same rights as the SPCA in terms of the Animal Protection Act to remove animals from the public. The vet who has written numerous reports on her and has the reports from her own vet all saying she should not have cats or dogs will speak. We have voice messages from her daughter saying her mom paid for the bond of the property using the donation money - that is their house? And they don't have books? We will speak to 3 animals organizations about the abuse, we will speak to a first responder about what happened that night, and eye-witnesses about what they saw.

I interviewed "Joseph" - a staff member who worked there for several years who was made to work for less than R75 per day. He said the animals were suffering always, always sick with oozing eyes, dying etc, dogs were always fighting, sometimes to the death, and she made him bury them all the time. He said she doesn't care about the animals, only the money, and he said she often was never there. Lindie says she is just being portrayed as a monster, but really she just has the animals best interests at heart - the evidence from the SPCA's files shows otherwise. Please see timeline of all the inspections below:

2012:
3 feb 2012 – dachshund – signed over attacked by other dogs.
Issued her a long warning on 3rd feb…. always the same… water, animals kept out of sun, no shade/netting – not enough kennels, number of animals – injury’s must be fixed, no fly control, fly bite on the ears… grass is long – fleas – infestation. Skin conditions… old feces, rotten bones should be removed. Fence fighting – separate – injuries… bite wounds, punctures… females on heat… made a video clip no 4feb209 (female on heat with 3 males dogs – after the fire). Too many non neutered dogs, recommended sterilized. Sick and injured animals – self medicated…
Even before fire – records – get from vet – but never did. Records burnt down… vet by law keeps records… to date have not received it. Cats and rabbits had growths, stitches not removed from previous sterilized animals… discharge – independent vet… diseases on property – enclosures – uses.
Kennels of dogs should be placed under shade… 33 cats in 2x3 enclosure with 3 litre boxes… 1 for 2 cats.
Vet and attorney – she’s qualified in animals protection act – why does SPCA have to come and tell you – she is aware? Why must we come and point it out from her – neglect… vet told her – do not use enclosures… healthy cats with sick cats – causes them to get sick. Borders 77- feline leukemia – not responsible. 3 cats here – snuffles -
7 feb 2012 – signed 12 cats over…. It was john van der merwe – he used to work at Irwin animal rescue centre, after the case, he moved from Irwin to purrpaws – kennel manager – kept in a wooden wendy house – poor condition – snuffles – upper respiratory disease, discharge from eyes…
More warning from van der bijl – 17 august 2012 – and 21 august 2012, 23 august 2012.
Vet’s report. Animal behaviourist.
Kitty and cat rescue – took animals .
AACL – were there – fully backing SPCA.

Vereeniging – relapse – drug addict – get relapse… fine… knows about sick animals…
Sold animals… horses.
2013
20 april 2013 – warrant – with photo’s. – 3 warning… problems with dogs who needed a vet, problem with animals, no de-worming – wendy house, vaccinations… no records…
Her daughter started in 2013 – welsh. Director.
Another warning 20/6/2013.
22 – 2013 – vet – 25 cats with snuffles, 4 eat mites, scratch injury ear mites, treated. Repeat infection euthanized. Snuffles – dormant. Eye – infection rion trachititis.
23 august 2013 – warrant van der bijl – warning.
Allegation of vets who give her meds without seeing animals. Vets report – snuffles cat

Went quiet – off the record – no one followed up. And the local SPCA – van der bijl – closed? Amalgamated in August 2015.

1 Feb 2016 – warning recommended no more cats allowed cos of disease. No more dogs cos of fighting. Fence fighting. Qualified veterinarians – self medicating… where is she getting medication? Parasites again, dogs struggle to walk. Majority of cats eye nasal discharge, snuffles… records kept again… date of admission.
Vet report – 11 march 2016
All felines must be tested for FIV, leukemia. No new cats should be introduced. Euthanize positive ones.
Another vets report
26 feb 2016
2/8 positive FIV and leukemia.
1 december 2016
Adequate food, vet treatment, grooming, dogs with skin conditions
27 october 2016
Lindi signed over non responsive cat – busy dying…

Monthly inspections – 27 jan follow up, 16 feb follow up, 5 july, 23 august, 26 august 2016, 27 oct, 8 nov, 1 dec. 29 dec 2016.
25 jan 2017, 2 march 2017, 30 march, 2017, 26 april, 23 may, 22 june, 27 july, 8 sept, 12 oct, 10 nov, 14 dec 2017
2018 – 12 jan, 8 feb, 9 feb, 15 march, 18 april, 7 may – no one there, 10 may, 22 june, 18 july, 15 august, 1 sept (recived a complaint from head office with cats dying – mia telling them) – lindi wasn’t at property, worker can see sick cats – not allowed on rest of property. 4 sept went back to check dogs, 25 sept, 30 oct warning issued – vet treatment, groom animals, treat internal external parasites, horses needed ferrier – underweight, cats underweight and sick, 2 nov, 20 nov 5 dec
8 jan 2019 – warning – food (underweight), provide vet treatment, clean environment, kennel numbers for treatment, cats needed treatment. 11 jan – follow up on vets report and treatment, dogs are underweight, bite wounds, self medicating animals (not against law – not against animal protections act to provide own animals – law…
Night of fire 30 jan…
In JAN Lucinda issued on 9, staff had a meeting, inspector dealing with case, enough is enough…
40 inspections… then the fire?

30 october 2019
AACL – 4 years – refused entry… until 5 – animals dying… her husband is a police officer… police station is in entrance in viljoen’s drift…

Fire –local police called spca – couldn’t deal with the situation. Billy went out, marlene went out, Candice, Lucinda, another cape town, arno inspectors – 6+ 2 volunteers.
Hostile – her lindi – chanelle (daughter) – just hear to kill animals. Station commander – said to chanlele – spca here to handle situation – evacuate animals – treatming…
Weekblad – (lady from er24 – furniture)
Elise templehoff – spoke to lindi – told her – two days before fire – pray – god send…
Cats that’s she removed with feral – antique furniture was out, tv screen – alleged only person in house, cats and dogs? ER will say it.
30 died – no one was allowed in – ER went in, fire brigade and police… forensics…
Final warning morning after fire.

Inspector – information…ppl were on property – animals were being taken from certain areas to purrpaws – feral cat society’s. Weren’t happy. Waiting for information – received statement. In court… inspector dealing with the people…

Script:


“Allen” : “Absolute chaos, ppl running around trying to get in, there was police officers trying to keep the people out, there was dogs screaming, cats going crazy…”
This was the scene on January 30th at PurrPaws for Life - an animal rescue centre near the Vaal river in the Free State. Although it was reported the shelter was on fire, it was only the house on the property but, rescue teams were concerned for the 1100 animals surrounding the house. Eye-witness “Allen” is speaking anonymously for fear of repercussions.
Allen: “On the side of the house, there was a couple of puppies that was lying on a table, one of those plastic tables, and they literally melted on the table.”
The fire ended the lives of roughly 30 animals, but animal welfare organizations stepped up to safely rehome the majority of the cats and dogs, leaving roughly 250 at the rescue centre. Donations flooded in to help the animals. But, that all changed when allegations of abuse and neglect began to swirl around the shelter’s owner Lindie Van Rooyen.
Marlien: “We found a horror scene where several cats were in the Wendy house.
Marlien De Klerk manages the Vereeniging & Vanderbijlpark SPCA. They began inspecting the animals that lived on the premises.
Marlien: “The cats had severe injuries, some of their eyes was popping out, there was actually one kitten that was busy dying inside the house.”
“Allen” : “Never from a shelter, have I seen anything that bad. It felt like hell.”
According to numerous witnesses the animals were diseased, had parasites, were emaciated, not neutered, and had wounds not associated with the fire.
Marlien: “As you can see there’s purple spray on the wounds, so lindie treated this dog before the night of the fire. The independent vet said that the dog was in such severe pain that he literally licked his own skin off.”
“Joseph,” a former employee, is speaking anonymously as he says he’s scared of Van Rooyen. He claims the neglect happened for the several years he worked there.
“Joseph”: “They don’t come sick, they get sick there. Some of the cats they’re starting to swell in the eyes. Ugh it gross.”
Sasha: “Did they suffer?”
“Joseph”: “They suffered. Esp when it comes to kittens…
It was Joseph’s job to bury the dead.
Sasha: “How many animals have died there?”
“Joseph”: “A lot, I can’t even remember how many, cos about every day we were burying them.”
He claims the majority of animals were not sterilized, leading to dogs fighting.
“Joseph”: “They’re overcrowded in the camps, when it’s eating time, they’re fighting. Some of them they’re dying from the fights.”
Rulof: “Information was coming to us about animals in bad conditions.”
Rulof Jackson is the chief inspector of the Animal Anti-Cruelty League or AACL. Together with the SPCA, they obtained a warrant to inspect PurrPaws for life several days after the fire.
Rulof: People have been sending through photo’s and so on, statements, conditions- not caused by fire.”
Over 80 animals were confiscated.
SEVERAL INDEPENDENT VETERINARY REPORTS HAVE CONFIRMED THE SPCA’S FINDINGS OF ALLEGED ANIMAL NEGLECT AND ABUSE AT PURRPAWS FOR LIFE.
The reports conclude that the majority of animals confiscated were not neutered, many were emaciated and infested with parasites and fleas, and some had diseases like Snuffles.
Marlien: “At some stages of the snuffles, the eyes would literally pop out, if they didn’t receive the treatment.”
Independent Veterinarian Dr. Faizel Suleyman explains the condition.
Vet: “So snuffles is a layman's term for a respiratory disease. There’s so much pusy discharge from the eyes, eventually the eyelids glue together, and their nostrils accrueded with puss.”
Claire: “But what if it goes untreated?”
Vet: “You have an animal that wastes away and eventually dies.”
Rulof: “The evidence shows neglect - will lead to abuse which is against the animal protection act.
SINCE 2016, THERE HAVE BEEN 40 SPCA INSPECTIONS ON PURRPAWS FOR LIFE, BUT THE ALLEGED ABUSE ON ANIMALS GOES BACK 7 YEARS.
Marlien: “In 2012 when we conducted inspections at the purrpaws for life shelter, the cats and kitten had severe snuffles.”
Since then, there have been 14 additional warnings says Sandton Senior Inspector Jaco Pieterse who was invited to assist by the local SPCA.
Jaco: “The warnings basically include contraventions of the Animals Protection Act where the shelter is notified of contraventions that they need to fix.”
LINDIE VAN ROOYEN HAS MAGISTERIAL RIGHTS - THE SAME AS THE SPCA - WHICH BASICALLY MEANS THAT SHE MUSN’T ONLY ABIDE BY THE ANIMAL RIGHTS ACT - SHE HAS THE POWER OF A POLICE OFFICER IN TERMS OF ENFORCING IT.
Jaco: “You should be the protector of animals and you should be the one preventing cruelty and not allowing animals to suffer.”
The problem is that animal welfare organisations are not required to register with any formal body. They only need to comply with Animal Protection Act and municipal by-laws - therefore there is little to no regulation. According to the SPCA, it’s as easy as registering a company and calling yourself a rescue centre.
Jaco: “Members of the public and companies donate to organizations in good faith assuming and trusting that the funds will be well spent and well managed. And when an organization has no proper financial management and controls in place. Red flags and alarms go off.”
We confronted van rooyen about these allegations at her shelter this week - she says her financials and records of the animals were all destroyed when her house burned down. It was alleged that she had received a R1 million rands in donations in money and donated items.
Lindie: “I'm so lucky if I had a million, can i go on holiday. Yes. I haven't been on holiday in three years.”
After rehoming the large majority of the animals, she claims she did not keep all the money for herself.
Lindie: “Just over R500,000, but I paid out two hundred and twenty thousand to the rescue centers that helped.
Claire: “You are a no kill shelter?”
Lindie: “Now I stipulated specifically no kill so that people can understand that we do not euthanize because we can't find homes. But I've unfortunately, yes I've had to euthanize dogs.”
Claire: “I need to know your shelter because that's a misleading misleading term?”
Lindie: “It’s a misleading term, but the problem is no kill is better understood than pro-life.”
Rulof: “People have this fantasy of animals running in the fields, being happy, all living happily together and so on. But that is not the reality that we have seen…”
Lindie: “Everything that I get in here is something that nobody else wants, about 80 percent of our dogs that come in here are very sad cases extremely emaciated in very bad shape.”
Van Rooyen insists the rescue has rehabilitated and rehomed animals - and these she claims are her success stories...
Lindie: “This is where we’ve made a difference. These were six puppies that were thrown away in a veld.”
Claire: “This one?”
Lindie: “Picked up as a stray. Nobody wanted him because he had an either, but at our expense we. Fixed his eye.”
She claims the cats found by the SPCA, after the fire, arrived sick.
Lindie: “The previous night somebody had done three boxes here. I'm talking about huge boxes filled with cats all sick but no idea of where they came from.”
Claire: “Are you saying that every single sick cat that was taken away from here was dumped at your doorstep 12 hours before?
Lindie: “It sounds weird and you know what. I could understand it. I said to the SPCA i’m not going to be able to care for these cats, please take them with you.”
Van Rooyen says she complies with the warnings, and denies they’re serious.
Lindie: “Several warnings, warnings of what? They’ve given me warnings about the kennels are skew or the blankets are outside.”
But some of the warnings were in fact for injured or sick animals. Although, mostly they were for the animals environment. Coincidentally the shelter was cleaned up for our appointment.
Claire: Why did we not shut the centre down?
Marlien: “The SPCA was building a case we have issued her them warnings in the past, we have to issue warnings… but this was literally the worst that we’ve sent the centre.”
Joseph says when the SPCA came, Lindie would allegedly hide the sick or injured animals.
Joseph: “When the these guys come, she’d see their bakkie, and then she took some of the animals from the camps. They were injured, some of them, they were sick, she’d put them in the one room, hiding them from them.”
Founder of Kitten and Cat Rescue Mia Kapp believes she came across THIS room called “the hospital.” She visited the shelter 4 times late last year.
Mia: “There was this shack and inside was just a nightmare. Most of the cats had no more hair left on their bodies, they were just dying, that’s where I removed a dead cat. Then I moved a door, a cat having seizures...
Mia: “This terrible, terrible, look what the cat looks like. This little cat is an adult, weighs 1.5 kg’s and it’s now been euthanized.”
Mia: “You put animal in there, and you advertise yourself as a no kill shelter, but it’s actually slow kill.”
We showed Van Rooyen some of the photo’s and videos.
Claire: “Do you recognize this cat?”
Lindie: My cats would never look like that.
Claire: There's another one. eyes a mess.”
Lindie: “Ooo ya, that’s those cats, that came in the night before.”
Claire: “These pictures are alleged to have been taken of animals before the fire…”
Producer: August last year? (subtitle)
Lindie: Ja, ja, no not before the fire?
Claire: (nods) Mhm mhm.
Lindie: That's interesting.
Claire: (nods) Mhm mhm.
Lindie: Well I didn't know that. Okay.”
C: People say these are the cats that you had here?
Lindie: “What if it was taken in August, last year, how does it end up now?”
Claire: “No, people have had the pictures, they took the pictures when they came.”
Lindie: mmm
Claire: “What would you say to that, is that person lying?”
Lindie: “Well I don't know who the person is and I'm not sure if it was taken here.”
Claire: “That’s bad Lindie.”
Lindie: “It is bad, but i’m not aware that it was here.”
While she insists she didn’t recognize the cats in the photo’s, she conceded the cats in these videos were from her shelter.
Lindie: “These were taken last year, when Kitten and Cat Rescue was here, when I laid a complaint against me because I was treating sick cats.
Claire: “Do you agree that seeing a cat like this. Suffering. Dying slowly is completely unacceptable?”
Lindie: “Yes it is. That could be anybody’s cat for all I know.”
Claire: “That’s cruelty though? That neglect is abuse.”
Lindie: “Claire, I cannot take responsibility for people dumping their sick animals here.”
Claire: “But you can take responsibility once the animal is only on your premises.
Lindie: “Yes.”
Despite the allegations, Van Rooyen says she’ll continue the facility, but she’ll no longer be keeping cats.
The SPCA laid charges of animal cruelty against the shelter. On Wednesday they came back with a warrant and further removed 21 animals - some of which were injured from fighting - even while they were there… (pause of dogs fighting)
Van Rooyen says the SPCA did not accept her vets report, but she will continue to operate until their allegations are proven true in a court of law. 12:12

2019 - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 15 March 2019 Script: “Allen” : “Absolute chaos, ppl running around trying to get in, there was police officers trying to keep the people out, there was dogs screaming, cats going crazy…” This was the scene on January 30th at PurrPaws for Life - an animal rescue centre near the Vaal river in the Free State. Although it was reported the shelter was on fire, it was only the house on the property but, rescue teams were concerned for the 1100 animals surrounding the house. Eye-witness “Allen” is speaking anonymously for fear of repercussions. Allen: “On the side of the house, there was a couple of puppies that was lying on a table, one of those plastic tables, and they literally melted on the table.” The fire ended the lives of roughly 30 animals, but animal welfare organizations stepped up to safely rehome the majority of the cats and dogs, leaving roughly 250 at the rescue centre. Donations flooded in to help the animals. But, that all changed when allegations of abuse and neglect began to swirl around the shelter’s owner Lindie Van Rooyen. Marlien: “We found a horror scene where several cats were in the Wendy house. Marlien De Klerk manages the Vereeniging & Vanderbijlpark SPCA. They began inspecting the animals that lived on the premises. Marlien: “The cats had severe injuries, some of their eyes was popping out, there was actually one kitten that was busy dying inside the house.” “Allen” : “Never from a shelter, have I seen anything that bad. It felt like hell.” According to numerous witnesses the animals were diseased, had parasites, were emaciated, not neutered, and had wounds not associated with the fire. Marlien: “As you can see there’s purple spray on the wounds, so lindie treated this dog before the night of the fire. The independent vet said that the dog was in such severe pain that he literally licked his own skin off.” “Joseph,” a former employee, is speaking anonymously as he says he’s scared of Van Rooyen. He claims the neglect happened for the several years he worked there. “Joseph”: “They don’t come sick, they get sick there. Some of the cats they’re starting to swell in the eyes. Ugh it gross.” Sasha: “Did they suffer?” “Joseph”: “They suffered. Esp when it comes to kittens… It was Joseph’s job to bury the dead. Sasha: “How many animals have died there?” “Joseph”: “A lot, I can’t even remember how many, cos about every day we were burying them.” He claims the majority of animals were not sterilized, leading to dogs fighting. “Joseph”: “They’re overcrowded in the camps, when it’s eating time, they’re fighting. Some of them they’re dying from the fights.” Rulof: “Information was coming to us about animals in bad conditions.” Rulof Jackson is the chief inspector of the Animal Anti-Cruelty League or AACL. Together with the SPCA, they obtained a warrant to inspect PurrPaws for life several days after the fire. Rulof: People have been sending through photo’s and so on, statements, conditions- not caused by fire.” Over 80 animals were confiscated. SEVERAL INDEPENDENT VETERINARY REPORTS HAVE CONFIRMED THE SPCA’S FINDINGS OF ALLEGED ANIMAL NEGLECT AND ABUSE AT PURRPAWS FOR LIFE. The reports conclude that the majority of animals confiscated were not neutered, many were emaciated and infested with parasites and fleas, and some had diseases like Snuffles. Marlien: “At some stages of the snuffles, the eyes would literally pop out, if they didn’t receive the treatment.” Independent Veterinarian Dr. Faizel Suleyman explains the condition. Vet: “So snuffles is a layman's term for a respiratory disease. There’s so much pusy discharge from the eyes, eventually the eyelids glue together, and their nostrils accrueded with puss.” Claire: “But what if it goes untreated?” Vet: “You have an animal that wastes away and eventually dies.” Rulof: “The evidence shows neglect - will lead to abuse which is against the animal protection act. SINCE 2016, THERE HAVE BEEN 40 SPCA INSPECTIONS ON PURRPAWS FOR LIFE, BUT THE ALLEGED ABUSE ON ANIMALS GOES BACK 7 YEARS. Marlien: “In 2012 when we conducted inspections at the purrpaws for life shelter, the cats and kitten had severe snuffles.” Since then, there have been 14 additional warnings says Sandton Senior Inspector Jaco Pieterse who was invited to assist by the local SPCA. Jaco: “The warnings basically include contraventions of the Animals Protection Act where the shelter is notified of contraventions that they need to fix.” LINDIE VAN ROOYEN HAS MAGISTERIAL RIGHTS - THE SAME AS THE SPCA - WHICH BASICALLY MEANS THAT SHE MUSN’T ONLY ABIDE BY THE ANIMAL RIGHTS ACT - SHE HAS THE POWER OF A POLICE OFFICER IN TERMS OF ENFORCING IT. Jaco: “You should be the protector of animals and you should be the one preventing cruelty and not allowing animals to suffer.” The problem is that animal welfare organisations are not required to register with any formal body. They only need to comply with Animal Protection Act and municipal by-laws - therefore there is little to no regulation. According to the SPCA, it’s as easy as registering a company and calling yourself a rescue centre. Jaco: “Members of the public and companies donate to organizations in good faith assuming and trusting that the funds will be well spent and well managed. And when an organization has no proper financial management and controls in place. Red flags and alarms go off.” We confronted van rooyen about these allegations at her shelter this week - she says her financials and records of the animals were all destroyed when her house burned down. It was alleged that she had received a R1 million rands in donations in money and donated items. Lindie: “I'm so lucky if I had a million, can i go on holiday. Yes. I haven't been on holiday in three years.” After rehoming the large majority of the animals, she claims she did not keep all the money for herself. Lindie: “Just over R500,000, but I paid out two hundred and twenty thousand to the rescue centers that helped. Claire: “You are a no kill shelter?” Lindie: “Now I stipulated specifically no kill so that people can understand that we do not euthanize because we can't find homes. But I've unfortunately, yes I've had to euthanize dogs.” Claire: “I need to know your shelter because that's a misleading misleading term?” Lindie: “It’s a misleading term, but the problem is no kill is better understood than pro-life.” Rulof: “People have this fantasy of animals running in the fields, being happy, all living happily together and so on. But that is not the reality that we have seen…” Lindie: “Everything that I get in here is something that nobody else wants, about 80 percent of our dogs that come in here are very sad cases extremely emaciated in very bad shape.” Van Rooyen insists the rescue has rehabilitated and rehomed animals - and these she claims are her success stories... Lindie: “This is where we’ve made a difference. These were six puppies that were thrown away in a veld.” Claire: “This one?” Lindie: “Picked up as a stray. Nobody wanted him because he had an either, but at our expense we. Fixed his eye.” She claims the cats found by the SPCA, after the fire, arrived sick. Lindie: “The previous night somebody had done three boxes here. I'm talking about huge boxes filled with cats all sick but no idea of where they came from.” Claire: “Are you saying that every single sick cat that was taken away from here was dumped at your doorstep 12 hours before? Lindie: “It sounds weird and you know what. I could understand it. I said to the SPCA i’m not going to be able to care for these cats, please take them with you.” Van Rooyen says she complies with the warnings, and denies they’re serious. Lindie: “Several warnings, warnings of what? They’ve given me warnings about the kennels are skew or the blankets are outside.” But some of the warnings were in fact for injured or sick animals. Although, mostly they were for the animals environment. Coincidentally the shelter was cleaned up for our appointment. Claire: Why did we not shut the centre down? Marlien: “The SPCA was building a case we have issued her them warnings in the past, we have to issue warnings… but this was literally the worst that we’ve sent the centre.” Joseph says when the SPCA came, Lindie would allegedly hide the sick or injured animals. Joseph: “When the these guys come, she’d see their bakkie, and then she took some of the animals from the camps. They were injured, some of them, they were sick, she’d put them in the one room, hiding them from them.” Founder of Kitten and Cat Rescue Mia Kapp believes she came across THIS room called “the hospital.” She visited the shelter 4 times late last year. Mia: “There was this shack and inside was just a nightmare. Most of the cats had no more hair left on their bodies, they were just dying, that’s where I removed a dead cat. Then I moved a door, a cat having seizures... Mia: “This terrible, terrible, look what the cat looks like. This little cat is an adult, weighs 1.5 kg’s and it’s now been euthanized.” Mia: “You put animal in there, and you advertise yourself as a no kill shelter, but it’s actually slow kill.” We showed Van Rooyen some of the photo’s and videos. Claire: “Do you recognize this cat?” Lindie: My cats would never look like that. Claire: There's another one. eyes a mess.” Lindie: “Ooo ya, that’s those cats, that came in the night before.” Claire: “These pictures are alleged to have been taken of animals before the fire…” Producer: August last year? (subtitle) Lindie: Ja, ja, no not before the fire? Claire: (nods) Mhm mhm. Lindie: That's interesting. Claire: (nods) Mhm mhm. Lindie: Well I didn't know that. Okay.” C: People say these are the cats that you had here? Lindie: “What if it was taken in August, last year, how does it end up now?” Claire: “No, people have had the pictures, they took the pictures when they came.” Lindie: mmm Claire: “What would you say to that, is that person lying?” Lindie: “Well I don't know who the person is and I'm not sure if it was taken here.” Claire: “That’s bad Lindie.” Lindie: “It is bad, but i’m not aware that it was here.” While she insists she didn’t recognize the cats in the photo’s, she conceded the cats in these videos were from her shelter. Lindie: “These were taken last year, when Kitten and Cat Rescue was here, when I laid a complaint against me because I was treating sick cats. Claire: “Do you agree that seeing a cat like this. Suffering. Dying slowly is completely unacceptable?” Lindie: “Yes it is. That could be anybody’s cat for all I know.” Claire: “That’s cruelty though? That neglect is abuse.” Lindie: “Claire, I cannot take responsibility for people dumping their sick animals here.” Claire: “But you can take responsibility once the animal is only on your premises. Lindie: “Yes.” Despite the allegations, Van Rooyen says she’ll continue the facility, but she’ll no longer be keeping cats. The SPCA laid charges of animal cruelty against the shelter. On Wednesday they came back with a warrant and further removed 21 animals - some of which were injured from fighting - even while they were there… (pause of dogs fighting) Van Rooyen says the SPCA did not accept her vets report, but she will continue to operate until their allegations are proven true in a court of law. 12:12

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Two weeks ago, an animals shelter South of Joburg burnt down - animals died, and donated began flowing in. But now allegations of years of serious abuse and,now, arson are swirling around the centre.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Carte Blanche investigates whether PurrPaws for life owner - Lindi van Rooyen - made hundreds of animals suffer years of abuse from willful neglect (2012-2019) - and then decided to end it all by setting her house on fire. We all know her story - on Jan 30 2019, it was reported that the shelter at PurrPaws burnt down killing roughly 30 animals, call for the public to come save the animals and make donations came in. Roughly a million is account for with online postings, but since then she has gotten rid of almost 800 animals. Allegations then began by various shelters who received these animals - that there were not neutered, were pregnant, were badly injured, were very diseased, malnourished. The questions began - how did the fire start, why did lindie have so much time to remove her personal animals from the house, her furniture, her TV etc, First responders said the workers said she was seen where the fire started shortly before it went up in flames, and that they had been sent to fix a fence at the bottom of the garden. Neighbours said she often wasn't there, and neglected the animals - often hiding injured/sick ones from the SPCA when they came for inspections. Turns out the SPCA have been investigating her for years responding to numerous complaints.
metadata.Summary: The SPCA has given us access to their files on her - years of abuse from 2012 - January 2019 - the warnings range from serious abuse - animals that are sick not getting veterinary care, hundreds of animals being put down etc continual sickness amongst animals - especially cats (snuffles, oozing eyes etc), dogs fighting and malnourished - she often has numerous dogs in different cages who fight and are then mortally injured. There are warnings (all acknowledged and signed by her) that show the issues brought up after the fire have been going on for years. Shortly after the fire Kitten and Cat rescue gave evidence of serious abuse of the cats - those photo's were posted by the SPCA in response to the public asking why they had not stepped in. Turns out they were intending to shut her down before the mysterious fire. About the fire - Lindie says it was caused in the upstairs linen room by rats chewing cables, but arson investigators were called to the scene. We will ask the police for an update on that investigation. Turns out, it wasn't the rescue centre that was on fire, but her personal house.
metadata.Further information: So her personal house shares all elec and water etc with the shelter, she has no books and has never produced even vet bills to the SPCA. When asked about it, she says she'll send them, but never does. She has received thousands of donations, but now has gotten rid of the majority of the animals. I went undercover and she said she will not close down, and will continue with the shelter, she told me she's highly allergic to cats, yet managed to get roughly 50-70 out of the house (living in the house) into cages before the fire?!? Against the vet's orders she has placed all the cats back into diseased cages, where non-diseased cats can get sick. She had continued operating and said she would continue regardless of the SPCA's allegations. She says she is being targeted by them, and that the animals were injured before they came. Numerous reports, evidence from numerous animal organizations and insider information all say and show otherwise. In fact, she asked for money as a donation so she can rebuild and reopen. She cannot say she didn't know because she has the same rights as the SPCA in terms of the Animal Protection Act to remove animals from the public. The vet who has written numerous reports on her and has the reports from her own vet all saying she should not have cats or dogs will speak. We have voice messages from her daughter saying her mom paid for the bond of the property using the donation money - that is their house? And they don't have books? We will speak to 3 animals organizations about the abuse, we will speak to a first responder about what happened that night, and eye-witnesses about what they saw. I interviewed "Joseph" - a staff member who worked there for several years who was made to work for less than R75 per day. He said the animals were suffering always, always sick with oozing eyes, dying etc, dogs were always fighting, sometimes to the death, and she made him bury them all the time. He said she doesn't care about the animals, only the money, and he said she often was never there. Lindie says she is just being portrayed as a monster, but really she just has the animals best interests at heart - the evidence from the SPCA's files shows otherwise.
